title: Patched Updater — label record
description: One application's structured verification and endpoint-authorization record. Endpoints currently execute the separately committed Installomator.sh label stanza; CI cross-checks the pkgindmg payload contract against that real runtime source. PAT-1403 owns the broader single-source migration. See docs/label-manifest-format.md.

label.description: Stable label id, kebab-case. Matches the source filename (engine/labels/<label>.json).

type.description: Artifact packaging type the engine must handle.

pkg_in_dmg.description: Optional only for type=pkgindmg. Absence is the root-unique-pkg default. An explicit object declares how the verifier and shell engine identify a non-default package inside the mounted DMG.

mode.description: The DMG must contain exactly one .pkg at its root. Nested packages are not candidates.
Match exactly one safe relative path/glob pattern inside the mounted DMG and require exactly one package result.
Select only the pattern for the verifier's current arm64/i386 rotation, matching the shell stanza's architecture branch.
Render one exact relative package path from a component of the resolved artifact version.

version_source.description: PAT-1385 P1 fix (round 8): which raw value the component split is applied to. 'resolved-version' is the same reportable version used for the up-to-date comparison (the long-standing default). 'sparkle-enclosure-version' instead uses the sparkle-appcast enclosure's own raw sparkle:version attribute -- ONLY meaningful when download.strategy is sparkle-appcast, and REQUIRED whenever the real shell stanza derives its pkgPathPattern component from `enclosure/@sparkle:version` rather than shortVersionString (jre8's Oracle feed is the case this exists for: sparkle:version="26" and sparkle:shortVersionString="1.8.501.0" are genuinely different strings, and using the wrong one silently diverges the verifier's rendered package path from what the shell actually installs). Required, not optional with a default, so any future label using this locator mode must explicitly state which XML source its path component comes from rather than inheriting an implicit, easy-to-get-wrong assumption.

mode.description: Render one exact relative package path by removing every non-digit character from the resolved artifact version.

app_path.description: Installed bundle path — used for the installed-version read and the post-install codesign Team ID check.

installed_version_key.description: Info.plist key used by the endpoint engine for the installed-version comparison. Absence means CFBundleShortVersionString, matching Installomator's default.

expected_team_id.description: The 10-character Apple Developer Team ID the artifact MUST be signed by. Must be present and non-empty — an empty value is rejected by CI (closes threat T4). Verified against Apple's records at review time.

download.description: How the engine and the verification agent obtain the installer.

url.description: Fixed HTTPS URL. May be a stable URL that server-side redirects to the current version.

strategy.description: How the real download URL is computed at run time. 'resolved' labels carry residual threat T5 until the app is moved onto the internal mirror.

source.description: The HTTPS endpoint queried to resolve the download URL (appcast XML, GitHub releases API, redirecting URL, vendor API).

asset_pattern.description: Optional regex/glob selecting the right asset from the resolved source (e.g. the macOS arm64 build).

vendor_api_referer.description: Optional HTTPS Referer header sent when resolving vendor-api URLs. Some CDNs use hotlink protection that requires a Referer from the vendor's own domain.

version.description: How the available (new) version string is determined, for the up-to-date comparison.

source.description: Where the available version string comes from. 'resolved-source' = extracted from the same response download.source returns (resolved labels). 'download-filename' = parsed from the artifact filename (static-redirect labels). 'http-headers' = Last-Modified/ETag heuristic. 'none' = not resolvable; the engine cannot pre-compare and treats the app as reinstall-on-request only.

pattern.description: Optional regex extracting the version from the source.

blocking_processes.description: Process names that must be quit before install. Empty array = none.

pinned_sha256.description: PAT-500: SHA-256 of the currently pinned mirrored artifact. Written by the mirror pipeline after a successful publish (ci/mirror_pipeline.py). Null until the first mirror run for this label completes. Endpoint verifies the downloaded artifact against this value when patched.mirror=true; a mismatch aborts the install.

max_artifact_bytes.description: PAT-662: per-label artifact size cap override in bytes. Null or absent = use the global 2 GB cap. Allows fine-grained size control for labels whose artifacts are known to exceed or should be bounded below the global cap.

cross_hash_sources.description: Independent hash oracles compared against the artifact SHA-256 after download (PAT-502). A mismatch is an alert; absence of a cross-source is not.

url.description: HTTPS URL returning a body that contains a SHA-256 hex string.

pattern.description: Optional regex to isolate the hash within the response body.

redistribution_notice.description: Licence notice that must accompany a redistributed mirrored binary. The mirror pipeline fetches the pinned notice, verifies its SHA-256, publishes it alongside the artifact, and records it in the public mirror manifest.

spdx.description: SPDX licence identifier, for example MIT or BSD-3-Clause.

url.description: Authoritative HTTPS source for the licence notice.

sha256.description: Pinned SHA-256 of the exact licence notice bytes.

patched.description: Patched-owned metadata — not part of the upstream label model.

allowlisted.description: True if endpoints receive this label. The endpoint allowlist is the subset of the manifest with allowlisted = true.

mirror.description: True if this app is served from the internal mirror rather than the vendor URL (review §4.4).

mirror_url.description: PAT-647: public CDN URL of the pinned mirrored artifact. Written by the mirror pipeline alongside pinned_sha256. Endpoint uses this URL instead of download.url when patched.mirror=true. Null until the first mirror run completes.

mirror_eula_approved.description: PAT-500: redistribution/redistribution-licensing confirmed for internal mirror. Must be true before the mirror pipeline will include this label. False = in scope for Phase 2 but EULA review pending. Set true only after per-label EULA sign-off.

vendor_only.description: PAT-664: true if this label cannot be mirrored programmatically — download requires session auth, CDN hotlink protection that cannot be replicated in CI, or the product has no public programmatic download URL. The mirror pipeline skips vendor_only=true labels and they do not appear in the failure report.

vendor_only_reason.description: PAT-664: human-readable explanation for vendor_only=true. E.g. 'auth-gated-cdn', 'vendor-api-unavailable', 'product-discontinued'. Required when vendor_only=true.

tier.description: Optional rollout grouping. 'core' = high-prevalence apps verified/mirrored first.

reviewed_by.description: Who last reviewed this label record.

reviewed_at.description: Date of last human review (ISO 8601 date).

notes.description: Free-text reviewer notes — e.g. redistribution-licensing status, URL-resolution caveats.

ring_policy.description: PAT-629: deployment ring policy override. 'immediate' = deploy to all rings on day 0, bypassing staged rollout. For security-critical apps (browsers, password managers) where rapid patching outweighs canary risk.

smoke_test_exempt.description: PAT-504: if true, the CI smoke test is skipped for this label. Requires smoke_test_exempt_reason.

smoke_test_exempt_reason.description: PAT-504: required when smoke_test_exempt=true. Explains why smoke testing is impractical (e.g. requires interactive login, no headless mode, requires hardware peripheral).

behavioral_exempt.description: PAT-505: if true, the behavioral analysis probe is skipped for this label. Requires behavioral_exempt_reason.

behavioral_exempt_reason.description: PAT-505: required when behavioral_exempt=true. Explains why behavioral analysis is impractical (e.g. kernel extension, requires hardware, produces high volumes of expected network noise).

behavioral_exceptions.description: PAT-505: known-good behavioral signals to suppress from alerts. Each key is a signal type; values are lists of allowed prefixes/names.

allowed_network_destinations.description: Remote host:port pairs (or prefixes) that are expected for this app and should not alert.

allowed_sensitive_paths.description: Sensitive filesystem paths this app legitimately writes to (e.g. a LaunchDaemon it owns).

allowed_unexpected_paths.description: Non-sensitive paths outside the expected app dirs that this app legitimately writes to.

allowed_persistence_plists.description: macOS: LaunchAgent/Daemon plist paths this app legitimately installs.

allowed_services.description: Windows: service names this app legitimately registers.

allowed_scheduled_tasks.description: Windows: scheduled task names this app legitimately registers.
